abstract: Evolutionary economics explains economic change through variation, selection, retention, transmission, innovation, and institutional transformation, whereas much of economics explains outcomes through purposive choice. This article argues that these modes of explanation become recursively connected once economic agents can represent the evolutionary processes in which they participate and intentionally alter their operation. It develops the concept of reflexive economic evolution: agents do not merely choose within given constraints or adapt to existing selection pressures, but can generate new possibilities, modify selection environments, organize transmission, and sometimes revise the criteria and mechanisms by which variants are selected. This latter second-order capacity is termed meta-selection. Reflexive economic evolution does not imply comprehensive control or a predetermined social end-state: guidance changes the distribution of possible trajectories under uncertainty rather than determining a trajectory. The framework shows how intentional and evolutionary explanations can be causally complementary, why effective agency is partly endogenous, and why policy should be understood not only as changing current outcomes but also as reshaping the evolutionary environment in which subsequent adaptation and innovation occur.
title: Beyond Optimization and Blind Selection: Reflexive Agency in Economic Evolution

abstract: How reliable are public debt statistics? This paper quantifies the magnitude, characteristics, and timing of hidden debt by tracking ex post revisions to sovereign debt statistics. We assemble a comprehensive new database of 119 editions, or vintages, of League of Nations, United Nations, IMF, and World Bank debt statistics, covering up to 187 countries over more than a century. We show that public debt is systematically underreported, with upward revisions averaging roughly one percent of GDP across advanced and developing economies, external and domestic debt, and all reporting systems we examine. Hidden debt accumulates in good times and tends to be revealed in bad times, often during IMF programs and sovereign defaults. Over the past one hundred years, nearly half of all sovereign defaults have coincided with substantial upward revisions to reported public debt. We incorporate these patterns into a quantitative sovereign default model and show that hidden debt raises default risk and borrowing costs, and thereby contributes to debt intolerance. Differences in the reliability of debt data across countries account for roughly 20% of the observed gap in debt-carrying capacity between low and high-income economies.
title: Hidden Debt Revelations

abstract: Agrodealers play a critical role in rural economies, selling essential inputs for agricultural production, stocking new products, and providing farmers with technical advice. However, uncertainty can discourage them from stocking newer, less familiar products, limiting the availability of innovative technologies and leading to market failures and low‐innovation equilibria. We provided Kenyan agrodealers with a 10% price discount on new, drought‐tolerant maize hybrids. The discount increased the likelihood that the agrodealer stocked the new hybrids and increased the share of the new hybrids in overall sales. In an information‐deprived environment, the discount encouraged dealers to gather more information about the seeds and increased agrodealers' sales effort.
title: Improving access to new technologies: An experiment with Kenyan input sellers

abstract: Using a state‐of‐the‐art structural gravity model, we investigate the impact of various (post‐)colonial cocoa trading arrangements on the cocoa trade between developing cocoa producer countries and rich industrial cocoa consumer nations in the time period 1951–1999. We find that in particular the trading arrangements of the European (Economic) Community (EEC/EC), such as the Association, Yaoundé and Lomé Agreements, as well as the UNCTAD International Cocoa Agreement, had a measurable positive impact on cocoa trade flows, in contrast to the British Commonwealth partnership or the GATT Generalised System of Preferences. In particular, the Yaoundé Agreement not only increased the trade between other EEC/EC members and the signatory cocoa producers, but also strengthened the trading relationship between the former coloniser countries and their cocoa producing former colonies, in fact more than offsetting the negative effect of independence.
title: International Cocoa Trading Arrangements Between Industrialised and Developing Countries 1951–1999: A Structural Gravity Analysis

abstract: Mandatory minimum (MM) sentencing is frequently identified as a driver of long sentences among federal drug offenders, but estimating its causal impact is complicated by prosecutorial discretion in charging. First, I show evidence of selective manipulation of MM eligibility, with prosecutors disproportionately choosing minority defendants for eligibility relative to comparable white defendants. This selection behavior creates bias in naive estimates of MM effects on sentence length. To recover the causal impact of MM eligibility, I use a regression discontinuity design with extrapolation that disentangles statutory effects from prosecutorial selection. I find that eligibility increases sentence length by approximately 10 months (14 percent) uniformly across case types, with no discernible heterogeneity across race. Together, these results indicate that racial disparities in MM sentencing arise primarily from prosecutorial charging decisions rather than from features of the statute itself.
title: How much do mandatory minimums matter?

abstract: Stock price delay serves as a key metric of information efficiency in stock markets, and identifying its determinants is essential for promoting market information efficiency. This study examines the effect of open public data (OPD) on stock price delay. Using the staggered adoption of city-level OPD portals in China as a quasi-natural experiment, our difference-in-differences analysis finds that OPD significantly reduces stock price delay, with an economic magnitude representing approximately 7.9% of its standard deviation. Cross-sectional analyses demonstrate that this effect is more pronounced when (1) public data on OPD portals are of higher quality, (2) public data are more relevant to firm operations, (3) public data are less substitutable, (4) investors have greater information processing capacity, and (5) firms’ information disclosure quality is lower. Additional tests show that OPD implementation is associated with improved liquidity, reduced return volatility, and diminished information content of earnings announcements. This study makes a valuable contribution to the literature on the determinants of stock price delay and the economic consequences of OPD, while offering insights for policymakers seeking to enhance market information efficiency and assess the effectiveness of OPD initiatives. 1 Under the Chinese institutional setting, a firm’s registered city generally coincides with the location of its headquarters rather than merely serving as a legal place of incorporation. According to the Company Law of the People’s Republic of China and the Regulations on the Administration of Market Entities Registration , a company’s registered domicile must correspond to the location of its principal administrative office, and firms relocating their principal office are required to update their registration accordingly (Chen, Hung, and Wang Citation 2018). Consequently, firms’ registered cities generally represent the locations of their headquarters. Because local governments in China play an active role in firms’ operations and are responsible for taxation, administrative approvals, industrial policy implementation, regulatory oversight, and other aspects of the local business environment (Xu Citation 2011), firms’ registered cities also represent the local institutional and information environments surrounding their headquarters. 3 GF Securities has developed an enterprise financial intelligent early-warning platform based on large-scale pre-trained models, which leverages public data and artificial intelligence to identify corporate financial risks at earlier stages and with greater accuracy. Similarly, the Shenzhen Stock Exchange’s blockchain-based industry risk data sharing project enhances the secure sharing of risk information across market participants, enabling investors to better assess industry-level risks. The Shanghai Equity Exchange has introduced a blockchain-based equity registration, custody, and transfer service platform that integrates multi-source data and provides more objective valuation benchmarks for investors in equity markets. Both the individual stock returns and the market returns used in Equation Eq. abstract: This study contributes to the literature on inequality of educational opportunity (IEOp) by advancing both the measurement and the empirical analysis of how social background shapes educational attainment in the United States over time. The study makes several key contributions. First, whereas existing studies typically rely on a limited set of circumstance variables, this study incorporates a more comprehensive and multidimensional set of background characteristics. Second, the paper introduces a novel composite measure – the Social Advantage Factor (SAF) – which summarizes multiple dimensions of social and economic background into a single index and overcomes the existing trade-off between capturing heterogeneity and maintaining statistical precision. Third, motivated by recent developments, this study employs machine-learning techniques to reduce reliance on ad hoc model selection, flexibly capture nonlinearities and interactions among circumstance variables, address multicollinearity, and enhance the robustness of opportunity estimates. In addition, this study provides a long-term perspective on inequality of educational opportunity by examining trends since 1920 across four distinct educational stages. The findings show that, over time, inequality of educational opportunity has decreased for ‘high school’ and ‘some college attainment’ levels. Evidence of persistent inequality remains at the college graduation level, while estimates for post-college attainment should be interpreted more cautiously due to weak model performance at this educational stage. KEYWORDS: Inequality educational opportunity Social Advantage Factor machine-learning JEL CLASSIFICATION: I24 I20 J18
abstract_zh: 本研究在推进教育机会不平等（IEOp）相关文献方面做出了贡献，既改进了测量方法，也深化了对美国社会背景如何随时间影响教育成就的实证分析。本研究具有多项关键贡献。首先，现有研究通常依赖有限的环境变量集，而本研究纳入了更为全面且多维的背景特征。其次，本文引入了一种新颖的复合测量指标——社会优势因子（SAF）——将社会与经济背景的多个维度汇总为单一指数，从而克服了在捕捉异质性与维持统计精度之间的现有权衡。第三，受近期研究进展启发，本研究采用机器学习技术，以减少对临时模型选择的依赖，灵活捕捉环境变量间的非线性关系与交互效应，处理多重共线性问题，并增强机会估计的稳健性。此外，本研究通过考察自1920年以来四个不同教育阶段的趋势，提供了教育机会不平等的长期视角。研究结果显示，随着时间的推移，“高中”和“部分大学教育”阶段的教育机会不平等有所下降。大学本科毕业阶段仍存在持续不平等的证据，而研究生及以上教育阶段的估计结果应更为谨慎地解读，因为该教育阶段的模型表现较弱。关键词：教育机会不平等 社会优势因子 机器学习 JEL分类：I24 I20 J18
title: The evolution of inequality of educational opportunity in USA: a machine-learning approach
title_zh: 美国教育机会不平等演变：一种机器学习方法

abstract: Consider the problem of designing a revenue-optimal auction mechanism when two heterogeneous items are sold to a single buyer having independent valuations over the items. The distributions of the buyer’s valuation for the items are assumed to have densities that are positive, nondecreasing, and continuously differentiable on their support sets [ c i , c i + b i ] in the positive axis. I prove that the optimal mechanism is deterministic if at least one of the minimum valuations (i.e., either c 1 or c 2 ) is sufficiently high. I provide a method to calculate the threshold of ( c 1 , c 2 ) beyond which the optimal mechanism is deterministic. I also provide a sufficient condition on the distributions of buyer’s valuations for which the individual sale mechanism is optimal. I show that when c 1 is low and c 2 is high, it is optimal for the seller to sell item 2 at the minimum valuation c 2 , thus effectively reducing the problem to finding the optimal mechanism in the one-dimensional setting only for item 1. I conjecture with promising preliminary results that this result can be extended to the three-item setting. Specifically, I conjecture that when c 1 and c 2 are low but c 3 is high, it is optimal for the seller to sell item 3 at the minimum valuation c 3 , thus effectively reducing the problem to finding the optimal mechanism in the two-dimensional setting for items 1 and 2.
abstract_zh: 考虑在将两种异质商品出售给对商品具有独立估值的单一买家时，设计收益最优拍卖机制的问题。假设买家对商品的估值分布具有正密度、非递减且在支撑集[ci, ci + bi]（位于正半轴）上连续可微。我证明，如果至少一个最低估值（即c1或c2）足够高，则最优机制是确定性的。我提供了一种方法来计算(c1, c2)的阈值，超过该阈值后最优机制即为确定性的。我还给出了买家估值分布的一个充分条件，在该条件下，单独销售机制是最优的。我表明，当c1较低而c2较高时，卖家以最低估值c2出售商品2是最优的，从而有效地将问题简化为仅针对商品1的一维设置中的最优机制求解。我推测，基于有前景的初步结果，这一结论可以扩展到三商品设置。具体而言，我推测当c1和c2较低但c3较高时，卖家以最低估值c3出售商品3是最优的，从而有效地将问题简化为针对商品1和2的二维设置中的最优机制求解。
title: On deterministic optimal mechanisms in a two-item setting for distributions with nondecreasing density
title_zh: 确定性最优机制：两物品情形下非递减密度分布的研究

abstract: We explore the use of Revelio data—obtained primarily from LinkedIn profiles—as a source of labor force microdata in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where large-sample, high-frequency, employer-linked alternatives are largely unavailable. To address the selection inherent to LinkedIn usership, we employ ILO labor statistics to construct five sets of country-year-specific weights that alleviate non-representativeness across occupation, industry, occupation × education, industry × education, and industry × firm-size cells. We further validate these weights using national census data where they are available and not used for ILO labor statistics. The weighted dataset provides a balanced monthly panel with coverage across most LMICs. We also discuss remaining limitations of the dataset, including within-cell selection and self-reporting errors, and suggest techniques to alleviate them. Despite imperfect coverage, Revelio offers improved temporal and geographical resolution as well as cross-country comparability and is especially useful for studying the role of firms in economic development.
abstract_zh: 我们探讨了利用Revelio数据——主要源自LinkedIn个人资料——作为低收入和中等收入国家劳动力微观数据来源的可能性，在这些国家，大规模、高频、与雇主关联的替代数据基本不可得。为应对LinkedIn用户群体固有的选择性偏差，我们采用国际劳工组织的劳动统计资料，构建了五组按国家-年份特定的权重，以缓解在职业、行业、职业×教育、行业×教育及行业×企业规模等分类上的非代表性。我们还利用可获取且未用于国际劳工组织统计的国家人口普查数据，对这些权重进行了进一步验证。加权后的数据集提供了一个覆盖大多数低收入和中等收入国家的平衡月度面板。我们还讨论了数据集现存的其他局限，包括单元内选择及自我报告误差，并提出了缓解这些问题的技术方法。尽管覆盖并非完美，Revelio数据在时间与地理分辨率上有所提升，并增强了跨国可比性，尤其适用于研究企业在经济发展中的作用。
title: From LinkedIn to Labor Statistics: Using Revelio Microdata for Labor Market Research in Developing Economies
title_zh: 从领英到劳动统计：利用Revelio微观数据研究发展中经济体的劳动力市场

abstract: We examine whether disproportionate insider control, or the divergence between insider voting and cash flow rights at dual-class firms, influences the extent to which stock price reflects information about future firm performance. We find that current returns incorporate less information about future earnings and cash flows as disproportionate insider control increases. However, monitoring by influential institutional investors, strong board oversight, and high-quality disclosure significantly attenuate this effect, such that disproportionate insider control does not result in less informative stock prices. Collectively, our findings reveal that, although the dual-class structure is associated with less informative stock prices, on average, monitoring and disclosure can alleviate investor concerns about disproportionate insider control while allowing firms to take advantage of the benefits of a dual-class ownership structure.
abstract_zh: 我们考察了双重股权结构公司中不成比例的内部人控制，即内部人投票权与现金流权之间的差异，是否影响股价反映未来公司业绩信息的程度。研究发现，随着不成比例的内部人控制增强，当前收益对未来盈利和现金流信息的包含程度降低。然而，有影响力的机构投资者监督、强有力的董事会监管以及高质量的信息披露显著削弱了这一效应，使得不成比例的内部人控制不会导致股价信息含量降低。总体而言，我们的研究结果表明，尽管双重股权结构平均而言与股价信息含量较低相关，但监督和披露能够缓解投资者对不成比例内部人控制的担忧，同时使企业能够利用双重股权结构带来的优势。
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
title: The informativeness of stock price at dual-class firms
title_zh: 双重股权结构公司股票价格的信息含量

abstract: Climate change and the transition to net zero are reshaping the macroeconomy, with important implications for monetary policymakers’ core price-stability objectives. As physical hazards become more frequent and severe, and as governments’ mitigation policies reallocate resources across the economy, central banks may increasingly face challenging trade-offs between stabilising inflation and supporting output. This column discusses the implications of climate change for monetary policy, including its effects on inflation, output, monetary transmission, structural economic factors and central bank communications. It introduces a practical framework for central banks as they assess, respond to, and communicate about climate-related shocks.
abstract_zh: 气候变化及向净零排放的转型正在重塑宏观经济，对货币政策制定者的核心价格稳定目标产生重要影响。随着物理危害日益频繁和严重，以及政府减缓政策在经济中重新分配资源，中央银行可能越来越面临在稳定通胀与支持产出之间的艰难权衡。本文探讨了气候变化对货币政策的影响，包括其对通胀、产出、货币传导机制、结构性经济因素及中央银行沟通的作用。文章为中央银行评估、应对及沟通气候相关冲击提供了一个实用框架。
authors: Solveig K. Erlandsen, Sui-Jade Ho, Danae Kyriakopoulou, James Talbot, Edwin Millar
title: The implications of climate change for monetary policy
title_zh: 气候变化对货币政策的影响

abstract: Standard portfolio theory predicts strong investor responses to changes in the equity premium, but empirical evidence has found much lower sensitivity. This column studies the effects of changes in the Norwegian wealth tax, which generated variation in the after-tax equity premium. It finds that investors adjusted strongly, but slowly, with adjustment continuing for several years. This is consistent with the presence of adjustment frictions, such as attention or information costs. The findings can also help reconcile household portfolio behaviour with standard levels of risk aversion.
abstract_zh: 标准投资组合理论预测投资者会对股权溢价变化作出强烈反应，但实证证据显示其敏感度远低于此。本文研究了挪威财富税变动的影响，该变动导致了税后股权溢价的差异。研究发现，投资者调整幅度显著但过程缓慢，调整持续数年之久。这与调整摩擦的存在相符，如注意力或信息成本。这些发现也有助于调和家庭投资组合行为与标准风险厌恶水平之间的关系。
authors: Andreas Fagereng, Luigi Guiso, Marius Ring
title: New evidence of strong but slow portfolio responses to equity premium changes
title_zh: 股票溢价变化下投资组合反应强烈但缓慢的新证据

abstract: Solar and wind power account for a growing share of electricity generation in China and now dominate new capacity additions. As the power system transitions toward renewable generation, greater flexibility will be required to maintain system stability. This paper uses a computable general equilibrium model to assess the macroeconomic implications of this transition. Model results indicate a modest increase in electricity prices in the near-term, followed by sustained declines as renewable shares rise, particularly when variability is managed through battery storage rather than coal-fired backup generation. While the transition requires substantial adjustments in electricity supply and investment, it raises GDP in the long run and strengthens energy security. Battery-based flexibility outperforms continued reliance on coal across multiple dimensions, even when accounting for rising electricity demand from emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. However, this transition pathway also increases the risk of stranded assets in the coal power sector.
authors: Hugo Rojas-Romagosa & Gregor Schwerhoff & Sneha D Thube & Sha Yu

title: Macroeconomic Impacts of China’s Energy Transition

abstract: This paper analyzes the credit-growth nexus by shifting the focus from aggregate leverage and credit stocks to new credit flows. Using quarterly data for 12 euro area countries over 2007–24, covering 96 percent of euro area GDP, the analysis shows a robust empirical association between newly granted bank credit and private final domestic demand (PFDD), a close proxy for GDP. A 10 percent increase in new private credit is associated with about 0.5–0.7 percentage points growth in PFDD. In contrast, specifications based on credit stocks or leverage produce unstable or counterintuitive estimates, reflecting measurement biases related to debt repayments and denominator effects. Nothwithstanding the importance of debt levels and leverage for financial stability and through debt service for the economy, the findings suggest that new credit flows appear to provide a more empirically reliable proxy for the macroeconomic role of bank lending.
title: Rethinking the Credit-Growth Nexus: New Credit Flows and Private Demand in the Euro Area

abstract: Whether exporters can take advantage of increases in foreign demand depends on the scalability of their input suppliers—that is, suppliers’ ability to expand production when demand rises. Using bilateral trade data linked to international input-output tables, I measure supplier scalability at the country-industry level and examine how it shapes downstream export growth. I find that supplier scalability varies sharply across industries within countries, that scalable suppliers tend to be connected to scalable suppliers themselves, and that downstream country-sectors exposed to more scalable suppliers respond more strongly to positive foreign demand shocks in sectors with relationship-sticky inputs. I rationalize these facts in a multicountry, multi-sector general-equilibrium trade model with input-output linkages, heterogeneous upward-sloping supplier supply curves, and gradually adjusting sourcing relationships. In the calibrated model, supplier bottlenecks substantially attenuate the export and welfare gains from a global demand expansion, while relationship stickiness determines where bottlenecks bind. Counterfactuals show that supplier upgrading and pre-arranged access to flexible sourcing networks are most valuable when targeted toward economically central, relationship-sticky, and bottleneck-exposed parts of the production network.

title: Scalable Suppliers in Global Trade Networks

abstract: We augment the two-country DSGE model from Mandelman and Zlate (2012) with endogenous migration of both skilled and unskilled labor, and analyze the economic impact of restricting migration for each type of labor on the migrants’ source and host countries. We calibrate the model with data for Guatemala and the U.S. as the source and host countries respectively. Restricting unskilled immigration has a more severe contractionary impact on the host economy than restricting skilled migration—reducing aggregate output by approximately 1 percent and consumption by 0.6 percent compared to the steady state—, given that in the steady state a lot more unskilled migrants are needed in the production function. Restricting unskilled immigration impacts negatively skilled immigration flows, but not vice versa, and it has a significant overall impact on the source economy, with aggregate consumption and income declining (mostly due to a fall in remittances). Our findings also highlight a key policy trade-off for the host economy: while a restrictive immigration policy (especially for unskilled labor) could reduce wage inequality by compressing the skill premium—raising host-country unskilled wages by 8 percent while lowering skilled wages by 1 percent compared to the steady state—, and could increase output per capita, it comes at the cost of lower overall economic activity and aggregate consumption. Moreover, by increasing the wage gap for unskilled labor between host and source economies, it also raises incentives for immigration, despite the increased cost of migration.
authors: Ms. Alina Carare & Metodij Hadzi-Vaskov & Jessie Kilembe & Felipe Leal
title: Assessing the Impact of Restricting Skilled and Unskilled Migration: A General Equilibrium Approach

abstract: This paper studies market power in Mexican industries over the period 2008-23 using establishment-level data from the Mexican Economic Census. We document a substantial increase in the average price markup over marginal costs, from 12 percent in 2008 to 27 percent in 2023. The sources of this increase vary across sectors and time: services, particularly wholesale and retail trade, account for most of the increase in markups until 2018, while manufacturing, led by transportation equipment and export-oriented industries, plays a larger role in more recent years. Rising markups in services are associated with greater local labor market concentration, suggestive of increasing monopsony power. In manufacturing, markup growth is linked to higher capital expenditure, consistent with firms sustaining larger markups to recover higher fixed costs. Moreover, rising markups in manufacturing are positively associated with total factor productivity, whereas in services they are uncorrelated with productivity. Overall, these findings suggest that while market power has increased over time, its underlying drivers have shifted from monopsonistic power in labor markets to higher fixed costs, with more favorable efficiency implications in recent years.
authors: Francisco Arizala & Diana Ricciulli-Marín & Johanna Schauer
